2054	    @classmethod
2055	    def _load_entities(
2056	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
2057	    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, object]], list[dict[str, object]]]:
2058	        raw_robots = cls._require_field(data, "robots")
2059	        raw_tasks = cls._require_field(data, "tasks")
2060	        if not isinstance(raw_robots, list):
2061	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'robots' must be a list")
2062	        if not isinstance(raw_tasks, list):
2063	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'tasks' must be a list")
2064	
2065	        robot_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2066	        robot_ids: set[str] = set()
2067	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_robots):
2068	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
2069	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} must be an object")
2070	            robot_id = record.get("robot_id")
2071	            if not isinstance(robot_id, str):
2072	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} field 'robot_id' must be a string")
2073	            if robot_id in robot_ids:
2074	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate robot id {robot_id!r} in checkpoint")
2075	            robot_ids.add(robot_id)
2076	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
2077	            if task_id is not None and not isinstance(task_id, str):
2078	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'task_id' must be a string or null")
2079	            if "position" not in record:
2080	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'position'")
2081	            route = record.get("route")
2082	            if not isinstance(route, list):
2083	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'route' must be a list")
2084	            if "distance_travelled" not in record:
2085	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'distance_travelled'")
2086	            robot_records.append(record)
2087	
2088	        task_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2089	        task_ids: set[str] = set()
2090	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_tasks):
2091	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
2092	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} must be an object")
2093	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
2094	            if not isinstance(task_id, str):
2095	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} field 'task_id' must be a string")
2096	            if task_id in task_ids:
2097	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate task id {task_id!r} in checkpoint")
2098	            task_ids.add(task_id)
2099	            assigned = record.get("assigned_robot")
2100	            if assigned is not None and not isinstance(assigned, str):
2101	                raise ValueError(
2102	                    f"task {task_id!r} field 'assigned_robot' must be a string or null"
2103	                )
2104	            if not isinstance(record.get("picked_up"), bool):
2105	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'picked_up' must be a boolean")
2106	            if not isinstance(record.get("completed"), bool):
2107	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'completed' must be a boolean")
2108	            if "pickup" not in record:
2109	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'pickup'")
2110	            if "dropoff" not in record:
2111	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'dropoff'")
2112	            task_records.append(record)
2113	
2114	        positions = [
2115	            tuple(record["position"])
2116	            for record in robot_records
2117	            if isinstance(record["position"], list)
2118	            and len(record["position"]) == 2
2119	            and all(_is_int(value) for value in record["position"])
2120	        ]
2121	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
2122	            raise ValueError("checkpoint robots cannot share a position")

2137	    @classmethod
2138	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2139	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
2140	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
2141	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
2142	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2143	        last_tick = -1
2144	        last_sequence = 0
2145	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
2146	            context = f"map change {index}"
2147	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
2148	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
2149	            tick = frame.get("tick")
2150	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
2151	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
2152	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
2153	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
2154	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
2155	            if sequence != index + 1:
2156	                raise ValueError(
2157	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
2158	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
2159	                )
2160	            if tick < last_tick:
2161	                raise ValueError(
2162	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
2163	                )
2164	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
2165	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
2166	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
2167	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
2168	            if not added and not removed:
2169	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
2170	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
2171	            if overlap:
2172	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
2173	                raise ValueError(
2174	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
2175	                )
2176	            changes.append(
2177	                {
2178	                    "type": "map_change",
2179	                    "tick": tick,
2180	                    "sequence": sequence,
2181	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
2182	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
2183	                }
2184	            )
2185	            last_tick = tick
2186	            last_sequence = sequence
2187	        return changes

2189	    @classmethod
2190	    def _validate_map_history(
2191	        cls,
2192	        base_grid: GridMap,
2193	        saved_grid: GridMap,
2194	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2195	    ) -> None:
2196	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2197	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
2198	        for frame in changes:
2199	            for key in ("added", "removed"):

2228	    @staticmethod
2229	    def _history_closed_cells(
2230	        base_grid: GridMap,
2231	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2232	    ) -> frozenset[Position]:
2233	        """Cells open on the base map that the recorded edits net-close.
2234	
2235	        The change history is replayed from *base_grid* (its validity and
2236	        reproduction of the saved grid are checked separately by
2237	        :meth:`_validate_map_history`), and the result holds exactly the cells
2238	        a preset-route robot may legitimately still name while waiting: open
2239	        in the initial map, closed later by an accepted edit, and still closed
2240	        at save time. A cell closed and reopened before the save nets to open
2241	        and is therefore absent, as is every base-map obstacle.
2242	        """
2243	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2244	        for frame in changes:
2245	            obstacles.update(tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"])

2378	    @staticmethod
2379	    def _validate_active_task_routes(
2380	        paused: set[str],
2381	        task_by_id: Mapping[str, Task],
2382	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
2383	    ) -> None:
2384	        """Reject routes that cannot finish the task each robot is bound to.
2385	
2386	        Traversability and adjacency are checked elsewhere. This enforces the
2387	        pickup/delivery business rules -- the very same waypoint requirement
2388	        :func:`_task_route_waypoints` plans with -- for tasks that are
2389	        assigned, unfinished and not paused by map unreachability: a non-empty
2390	        route must end at the dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet
2391	        -- and is not already standing on the pickup cell -- must still pass
2392	        through the pickup. Passing the dropoff early changes nothing; the
2393	        route only has to reach the pickup and return, and saved avoidance
2394	        detours need not match a replanned shortest route. Empty routes are
2395	        legal only when no remaining waypoint is required: the loaded robot is
2396	        already at the dropoff, or position, pickup and dropoff all coincide
2397	        (the goods are collected on resume). Paused tasks keep their empty-route
2398	        exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not judged as work in
2399	        progress.
2400	        """
2401	        for task in task_by_id.values():
2402	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
2403	                continue
2404	            if task.task_id in paused:
2405	                # Map-unreachability pauses legitimately carry an empty route
2406	                # regardless of pickup state; the binding itself is all that
2407	                # must survive.
2408	                continue
2409	            robot = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
2410	            if robot is None or robot.task_id != task.task_id:
2411	                # Ownership mismatches of this kind are reported separately.
2412	                continue
2413	            route = robot.route
2414	            label = (
2415	                f"task {task.task_id!r} assigned to robot {robot.robot_id!r}"
2416	            )
2417	            required = _task_route_waypoints(robot.position, task)
2418	            if route:
2419	                if route[-1] != task.dropoff:
2420	                    raise ValueError(
2421	                        f"{label} has a remaining route that ends at "
2422	                        f"{list(route[-1])} instead of its dropoff "
2423	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2424	                    )
2425	                if task.pickup in required and task.pickup not in route:
2426	                    raise ValueError(
2427	                        f"{label} has not picked up the goods and its remaining "
2428	                        f"route never reaches the pickup point "
2429	                        f"{list(task.pickup)} on the way to its dropoff "
2430	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2431	                    )
2432	            elif task.picked_up:
2433	                if robot.position != task.dropoff:
2434	                    raise ValueError(
2435	                        f"{label} has an empty remaining route with the goods "
2436	                        f"already picked up but the robot is at "
2437	                        f"{list(robot.position)}, not at the dropoff "
2438	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2439	                    )
2440	            elif required:
2441	                raise ValueError(
2442	                    f"{label} has an empty remaining route before pickup: the "
2443	                    "task can only resume when the robot position, pickup "
2444	                    f"{list(task.pickup)} and dropoff {list(task.dropoff)} all "
2445	                    "coincide"
2446	                )

2448	    @classmethod
2449	    def _iter_replay_events(
2450	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
2451	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[int, dict[str, object], object]]:
2452	        """Yield ``(index, frame, frame_type)`` for every replay event in order.
2453	
2454	        This is the single place that owns the ordinary-tick-frame rules both
2455	        format versions share, so they are never maintained twice: the
2456	        ``replay`` field must be a list, every frame must be an object, a
2457	        missing ``type`` means an ordinary tick frame, and tick frames must be
2458	        numbered consecutively from 1 -- map-change events sit between ticks
2459	        without consuming a number -- with a well-formed payload (checked via
2460	        the equally shared :meth:`_validate_tick_frame_payload`). Anything
2461	        beyond that stays with the two loaders: version 1 rejects non-tick
2462	        frames and normalizes the ``type`` field, version 2 keeps its own
2463	        event-type dispatch and map-change ordering checks. The scan is lazy,
2464	        so each frame is examined exactly when the consuming loader reaches it
2465	        and the first problem is reported in the same order as before.
2466	        """
2467	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "replay")
2468	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
2469	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'replay' must be a list")
2470	        tick_index = 0
2471	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
2472	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
2473	                raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} must be an object")
2474	            frame_type = frame.get("type", "tick")
2475	            if frame_type == "tick":
2476	                tick_index += 1
2477	                frame_tick = frame.get("tick")
2478	                if not _is_int(frame_tick):
2479	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} field 'tick' must be an integer")
2480	                if frame_tick != tick_index:
2481	                    raise ValueError(
2482	                        "replay tick numbers must run consecutively from 1; frame "
2483	                        f"{index} has tick {frame_tick}, expected {tick_index}"
2484	                    )
2485	                cls._validate_tick_frame_payload(frame, frame_tick)
2486	            yield index, frame, frame_type

2488	    @classmethod
2489	    def _load_replay(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2490	        replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2491	        tick_index = 0
2492	        last_map_tick = -1
2493	        last_map_sequence = 0
2494	        for index, frame, frame_type in cls._iter_replay_events(data):
2495	            if frame_type == "tick":
2496	                tick_index += 1
2497	                replay.append(frame)
2498	            elif frame_type == "map_change":
2499	                tick = frame.get("tick")
2500	                sequence = frame.get("sequence")
2501	                if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
2502	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change tick must be a non-negative integer")
2503	                if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
2504	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change sequence must be positive")
2505	                if tick != tick_index:
2506	                    raise ValueError(
2507	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is stamped tick {tick} but appears "
2508	                        f"after {tick_index} tick frames"
2509	                    )
2510	                if tick < last_map_tick or (
2511	                    tick == last_map_tick and sequence != last_map_sequence + 1
2512	                ):
2513	                    raise ValueError(
2514	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is out of order at tick {tick}"
2515	                    )
2516	                added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), f"replay frame {index}", "added")
2517	                removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), f"replay frame {index}", "removed")
2518	                replay.append(
2519	                    {
2520	                        "type": "map_change",
2521	                        "tick": tick,
2522	                        "sequence": sequence,
2523	                        "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
2524	                        "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
2525	                    }
2526	                )
2527	                last_map_tick = tick
2528	                last_map_sequence = sequence
2529	            else:
2530	                raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} has unknown type {frame_type!r}")
2531	        return replay

2572	    @classmethod

2574	        cls,

2577	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
2578	        base_grid: GridMap,
2579	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]] = (),
2580	    ) -> None:

2582	
2583	        Every tick frame is checked against the map in effect *during* that
2584	        tick: positions must be in bounds and traversable, no two robots may
2585	        share a cell, each robot may only wait or step one orthogonal cell
2586	        between consecutive tick frames, two robots may not swap cells within
2587	        one tick, and ``moved`` must list exactly the robots whose positions
2588	        changed.
2589	
2590	        Version 2 map changes take effect after the tick they are stamped on,
2591	        in their recorded order: the frame for tick *t* is judged against the
2592	        base grid plus every change stamped below *t*, then the changes stamped
2593	        *t* are applied and may not add obstacles onto cells frame *t* shows a
2594	        robot on -- even when a later change of the same tick removes the cell
2595	        again. Tick-0 changes precede the first frame. Adjacency is always
2596	        judged between neighboring tick frames; a map change between them never
2597	        moves a robot.
2598	
2599	        Version 1 files pass no changes, so the saved grid governs every frame.
2600	        The first frame has no recorded predecessor: its cells, overlaps and
2601	        ``moved`` ids are still checked, but neither the distance of the first
2602	        moves nor the first ``moved`` list is second-guessed.
2603	        """

2607	                f"replay has {len(tick_frames)} tick frames but the checkpoint is at tick {tick}"
2608	            )
2609	
2610	        expected_ids = set(robot_by_id)
2611	
2612	        def frame_positions(frame: Mapping[str, object]) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
2613	            raw = frame["robots"]
2614	            assert isinstance(raw, dict)

2616	                raise ValueError(
2617	                    f"replay frame {frame['tick']} robot ids do not match current robots"
2618	                )
2619	            return {robot_id: tuple(position) for robot_id, position in raw.items()}

2621	        # A non-zero-tick history must end exactly where the saved robots stand
2622	        # before any deeper history check runs.

2646	                sequence = change["sequence"]

2667	        # checkpoint is still at tick 0 the saved robot positions *are* the
2668	        # layout of that moment; otherwise they cannot be reconstructed.
2669	        initial_occupants = (
2670	            {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in robot_by_id.values()}
2671	            if tick == 0
2672	            else {}
2673	        )
2674	        apply_changes(0, initial_occupants)

2678	            frame_tick = frame["tick"]
